sections.title: Notable recent biology and biomedicine papers on arXiv — 2026-11-18 batch
sections.abstract:
Today’s configured biology/biomedicine listings yielded **9 selected papers** for the latest announcement batch (papers have UTC submission timestamps on 2026-11-16–17). The dominant pattern is machine-learning methods for spatial transcriptomics, perturbation biology, and molecular discovery, alongside mechanistic models and experimental validation. arXiv has no official trending chart; this is an inferred, evidence-ranked list from an incomplete preprint corpus, using category relevance, cross-list breadth, external discussion, journal status, and Semantic Scholar metadata—not downloads or readership.

Snapshot: 2026-11-18 17:17 UTC. Daily reporting uses the latest available announcement batch; no 2026-11-18 UTC-submitted API records were returned at snapshot time. Because attention evidence is sparse, this is titled **Notable recent papers**, not a measured popularity ranking.

sections.title: Discovery of new antiviral agents through artificial intelligence: in vitro and in vivo results
sections.abstract: A deep-reinforcement-learning platform generated 60,291 neuraminidase-targeting molecules; nine were selected for testing, and two inhibited influenza A/B neuraminidase and viral replication in cells, with activity also reported in mice.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report a computational-to-experimental pipeline, including enzyme, cell-based, and mouse studies; the arXiv record links an Antiviral Research 2024 article and DOI 10.1016/j.antiviral.2024.105818.
sections.unique_caveat: This is an accepted manuscript of a 2024 journal article rather than a new experimental result; the abstract does not establish human efficacy, safety, or clinical utility.

sections.title: Structured AI ideation yields physical strategies for epithelial barrier repair
sections.abstract: Abelio combines structured divergent/convergent AI ideation with literature search and refinement; the authors tested its proposed PEG and cholesterol-anchored complementary-DNA interventions in damaged Caco-2 monolayers.
sections.claimed_contribution: The paper reports benchmark comparisons against four frontier LLMs and cell-monolayer assays: PEG preserved barrier readouts, while complementary DNA produced sequence-specific and reversible effects.
sections.unique_caveat: The biological tests are in an in-vitro Caco-2 model; proposed PEG/DNA configurations are not directly observed, and the evaluation of scientific soundness includes an LLM judge.

sections.title: ST-FateFlow: Continuous Gene-Spatial Reconstruction with Differentiation-Potential Learning from Time-Resolved Spatial Transcriptomics
sections.abstract: ST-FateFlow uses structure-aware transport coupling and flow matching to interpolate gene-expression and spatial dynamics between unpaired time-resolved spatial-transcriptomics snapshots and learn a differentiation-associated potential.
sections.claimed_contribution: Across multiple public developmental and regenerative datasets, the authors report improvements in distributional and spatial interpolation metrics and consistency with known trajectories.
sections.unique_caveat: The method depends on cross-time coupling and registration quality and missing intermediate states; its potential is a relative ordering, not a fate probability or physical energy, and there are no new human or animal experiments.

sections.title: HoloGene: Learning to Lift Sliced Spatial Transcriptomics to Holistic 3D Gene Fields
sections.abstract: HoloGene models discontinuous spatial-transcriptomics sections as continuous 3D gene-expression fields with an anisotropic conditional implicit neural representation.
sections.claimed_contribution: Using held-out measured sections, the authors report better reconstruction accuracy and biological-preservation metrics than general-purpose INR and adapted spatial-transcriptomics baselines; code is linked.
sections.unique_caveat: The output is an inferred 3D field from sliced measurements, not direct observation of unsampled tissue; performance depends on registration, data distribution, and the held-out-section validation design.

sections.title: OCCAM: Improved Single-Cell Representation Learning and Perturbation Effect Prediction
sections.abstract: OCCAM is an MLP framework that combines denoising-based cell representations with gene-interaction, text, and protein-sequence features to predict genetic-perturbation effects across cell contexts and combinations.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report cross-context few-shot, held-out-cell-line, and double-perturbation comparisons against retrained competitors and simple baselines.
sections.unique_caveat: The paper says expression-level prediction remains challenging; reported gains are benchmark-model results, not evidence of biological or therapeutic effect in patients.

sections.title: Diversity Preservation Recovers Transcription Factor Motifs Across Challenging Confounder Landscapes
sections.abstract: The paper combines evolvable motif length with MAP-Elites diversity archives to improve transcription-factor motif recovery under confounding sequences.
sections.claimed_contribution: On five liver ChIP-seq datasets, the archives recovered target signals more reliably than a survivor-selection baseline and were comparable to or more robust than MEME in the reported settings.
sections.unique_caveat: Motif annotation remains difficult: neither method consistently ranks targets above close relatives for HNF4A and JUND across the full width range.

sections.title: Molecular memory reduces timing noise in stochastic gene expression
sections.abstract: Analytical and stochastic-simulation results indicate that multistep mRNA production and degradation can reduce first-passage-time noise in bursty gene-expression models through different mechanisms.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors derive small-noise-limit statistics and compare them with stochastic simulations beyond that approximation.
sections.unique_caveat: The claims are model-based and the analytical results have stated regime-of-validity limits; no biochemical or cellular experiment is reported.

sections.title: Rule-based curation and validation in batch fermentation of a genome-scale metabolic model of the mycoprotein fungus Fusarium venenatum A3/5
sections.abstract: The authors build and curate the iJL1143 genome-scale metabolic model for Fusarium venenatum A3/5 and validate it against four oxygen-enriched batch fermentations.
sections.claimed_contribution: Rule-based curation reduced mean final-biomass discrepancy from 20% to 6% against the draft model; adding a fitted lag time reduced biomass time-course error from 4.88 to 0.42 g/L.
sections.unique_caveat: Validation is limited to the reported strain, oxygen-enriched batch setting, substrates, and model comparisons; performance does not establish transfer to other feedstocks or production conditions.

sections.title: Optimising Recruitment and Sample Allocation in Multi-Site Rare Disease Studies
sections.abstract: A cardinality-optimisation framework allocates recruitment and metabolomic samples across sites while balancing yield, cost, capacity, and logistics.
sections.claimed_contribution: In simulated multi-centre scenarios for a project targeting 1,900 diagnosed patients across 24 centres and eight laboratories, the model maintained feasibility under constraints and reduced unconstrained metabolomic-analysis costs by about 30% versus heuristic baselines.
sections.unique_caveat: The evidence is simulation and operational modelling; it does not show that the allocation improves outcomes or recruitment in a completed clinical study.

sections.title: Trending Research Themes
sections.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics, AI-assisted molecular discovery, mechanistic modelling, and robustness under confounding recur across the selected corpus.

sections.title: Open Problems and Research Directions
sections.abstract: The selected papers support follow-up work on prospective spatial validation, independent replication of AI-generated molecular proposals, and transferability stress tests.

sections.title: Takeaway
sections.abstract: The clearest cluster is computational biology that reconstructs, predicts, or optimises biological systems, with limited but meaningful wet-lab validation.
